messages:
Maya: Hey team — GitOps CI started failing on helm lint for the gpu-nodepool chart. Error from ct job: 'values.schema.json: /gpu/count: Invalid type. Expected: integer, given: string'
Maya: Pipeline injects GPU_COUNT into values-override.yaml via envsubst, so the file ends up like:
```
gpu:
  count: "1"
  instanceType: nvidia-a100
```
Maya: Any quick fix? don't want to change env wiring across 12 repos.
Ryan: That is the JSON Schema validation step (helm 3.11 behavior). If envsubst yields quoted numbers, schema will complain. Two practical options: make the schema accept strings OR coerce to int in templates using "atoi".
Ryan: Example template usage: 
```
resources:
  gpu:
    count: {{ .Values.gpu.count | atoi }}
```
Jen: Important: many CI lint setups (chart-testing + ct:lint) run schema validation against the substituted values.yaml before templates are rendered, so runtime coercion in templates doesn't help the lint step.
Jen: In our pipeline ct runs: envsubst -> helm lint --values values-override.yaml, so schema sees the plain YAML.
Maya: Ah — so atoi fixes runtime but not lint. Thoughts on a single change that satisfies both?
Ryan: Best compromise: make values.schema.json accept both integer and string for that field, then coerce in templates for runtime safety. That keeps lint happy and still enforces numeric semantics when the chart is rendered.
Ryan: Schema snippet suggestion: 
```
"gpu": {
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "count": { "type": ["integer","string"], "minimum": 0 }
  }
}
```
Jen: Also double-check any helpers in templates/_helpers.tpl. Using include vs template can cause unintended quoting. Example bug we hit: 
```
{{- define "nodepool.labels" -}}
nodepool: {{ .Values.nodepool.name }}
{{- end -}}
```
If nodepool.name is numeric string, you might end up with unquoted label values. Prefer explicit formatting: `{{ .Values.nodepool.name | quote }}` when writing to metadata.labels.
Maya: We also surface GPU count into a ConfigMap consumed by the autoscaler which expects a string there, so templates sometimes need to wrap with quotes after atoi. ex: `gpu_count: "{{ .Values.gpu.count | atoi }}"`
CI Bot: DeployBot: ct logs attached: chart-testing/helm-lint failed with exit code 1; first error: values.schema.json: /gpu/count type mismatch.
Maya: If we relax schema to allow both, do we lose safety? I worry about accepting totally bogus strings like "one".
Ryan: Good point — extend schema with a pattern to allow only digits if string: `"pattern": "^[0-9]+$"` so schema permits strings but not arbitrary text. Example: 
```
"count": { "type": ["integer","string"], "pattern": "^[0-9]+$", "minimum": 0 }
```
That gives lint-time protection while allowing envsubst-produced strings.
Jen: Also add a small chart unittest or `ct lint` scenario that runs envsubst with typical env values to avoid regressions. We have a tiny script in infra-ci that does `envsubst < values-override.yaml | yq e -` — add that to the pipeline job.
Maya: Plan: 1) update values.schema.json to accept [integer,string] + pattern, 2) add `| atoi` in templates where we use numeric ops, 3) wrap labels/metadata with `| quote` to avoid unquoted integers, 4) add a ct test that uses ENV overrides. I'll open a PR.
Ryan: Also include a release note in the chart bump: "values.gpu.count accepts string env vars; templates coerce to integer" — helps ops teams.
Maya: One more thing — some repos use helmfile/helm-secrets and those tools sometimes keep env var values unquoted; we should audit the 3 repos that deploy GPU pools.
Jen: I'll add a quick grep job in infra-ci to list charts containing `gpu.count` and `nodepool` and post results in the PR.
Maya: Thanks. I'll draft the PR and tag @Ryan and @Jen for review. :+1:
Ryan: Happy to review.
Maya: Ping again when CI passes.
DeployBot: ct job rerun queued by Maya (manual).
